title: In 61 Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels sessions, task engagement decreased the axonal-wiring slope of fast inter-regional co-variation by 24%, as part of a proportional decrease of coupling
abstract: Question: does task engagement change how well the mesoscale axonal connectome predicts shared trial-to-trial variation between mouse brain regions? Data: Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels, 61 sessions (46 mice, 30 regions, 6,951 region pairs). Each session has an active change-detection block and a later passive replay of the same image sequence, recorded from the same neurons. Method: for each region we summed good-unit spikes 0-250 ms after each matched image flash (no changes, no licks), removed image means and slow drifts (about 90 s), and correlated regions (Fisher z) in each block. Wiring was the log10 Knox et al. (2019) normalized connection density. Models controlled for a distance spline, region terms and session terms; intervals came from 2,000 mouse bootstraps. The plan was written before passive coupling was computed. Results: wiring predicted coupling in both blocks (0.038 z per log10 density in the active block, 95% CI 0.031-0.046; 0.050 in the passive block, 0.041-0.060; positive in all 59 testable sessions). The active slope was smaller by 0.0118 (0.0072-0.0174), 24% of the passive value; 40 of 59 sessions agreed (Wilcoxon p = 0.004). The difference stayed after removal of running speed and pupil, with a firing-rate covariate, without drift removal and without region terms. The slope did not drift within either block; it changed at the block change. Strongly wired pairs (visual areas, LGd and LP with visual cortex, CA3 with CA1 and DG) lost the most coupling. Exploratory: active coupling was 0.64 times passive coupling of the same pair with no negative wiring term (+0.006, 0.001-0.010), so the data agree with a proportional decrease of fast coupling, not a selective loss of anatomical structure. The change did not follow reward rate or running change across sessions. Limitations: VBN block order is fixed, so engagement is confounded with elapsed time, satiety and the stimulus blocks between; 61 of 105 eligible sessions were used because of bandwidth (random order); the wiring is an unsigned tracer model from other mice.
